findings.summary: The refusal-word anchors ('refuse', 'refused', 'refusal', 'refusals') appear in almost every criterion of a job that adds a refusal rule, so the anchor does little in the only jobs that declare more than 25%.
findings.evidence: Jobs that change refusal rules write criteria like 'A test shows X is refused because Y' (see the current CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE at briefs.rs:1478 and this job's own criteria). Such a sentence has both a marker and an anchor but does not say why past readings should be refused. The plan accepts that the heuristic is only a floor because the verifier is shown the sentence. Fix: Anchor only on the past-reading phrases ('past/previous/earlier/older/accepted readings'), or prefer a reason in the same criterion as the declaration ('expected N% of newly refused readings because ...'). Keep the shown sentence as the verifier's check.

findings.summary: Taking the first matching item can show the verifier an unrelated sentence while the real reason appears later.
findings.evidence: The plan scans the criteria first, then out_of_scope, and stops at the first item that has a marker and an anchor. Criteria in a refusal-rule job often match before the out_of_scope reason the reader meant. Fix: Prefer, in this order: the criterion that carries the declaration, then out_of_scope items, then other criteria. Or show every matching item, capped, beside the list.
findings.location: Step 3 / Decision 2 ('first criterion or out_of_scope item')

findings.summary: The parser accepts only 'N% of newly refused', which narrows the accepted reading's 'expected N%' or 'N% of newly refused'.
findings.evidence: The accepted reading says the share is parsed from 'expected N%' or 'N% of newly refused'. The plan drops the bare 'expected N%' form, and gives a good reason: quoted test data, including this job's own criteria, would otherwise count as a declaration. The narrower form fails safe (held at 10%), and CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE teaches it. Fix: Keep the strict form. Name the narrowing in the change description and the CHANGELOG entry as a departure from the reading, so the user sees it.

summary: I read the snapshot to check the plan's references, and they all exist as described. In reading.rs: INTENDED_REFUSAL_PHRASES (line 2746), criteria_intend_higher_refusal (2758), replay_is_held(total, newly, intended: bool) (2774) and replay() taking criteria (2821/2857). In run/mod.rs: replay_view(&Replay) (157) and its only call at 2510, with replay_run reading ctx.reading.acceptance_criteria (2842). In briefs.rs: ReplayView, replay_section and CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE. The text at verify.rs:351 goes stale after the change. Replay::validate rejects held && intended (records.rs:2373), and Reading has out_of_scope (records.rs:465). The plan fixes the fault where it starts: the phrase exemption inside replay(). Having one helper, replay_declaration_of(&Reading), feed both the gate and the verifier view is the right design. Keeping intended = declared.is_some() && !held keeps old records valid without touching records.rs. Each demonstration calls the production parser, replay_is_held, replay and replay_view, and would fail under the base code. The marked_cases, base_checker and marker_candidate doubles only decide which cases refuse; they do not stand in for the rule under test. CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE is printed into the reader brief (briefs.rs:1637), which sits outside the budgeted sets, so the 1997-of-2000 reader budget is not at risk. There are no blocker or major findings. On soundness: the reason detector's refusal-word anchors are weak in exactly the jobs that would declare a high share, and taking the first matching item can show the verifier an unrelated sentence. The strict 'N% of newly refused' form narrows the accepted reading, but it fails safe and the plan says so openly. All of these are minor.
